prompts:
Create a production-oriented TRANSPARENT pixel-art weapon direction atlas for a top-down survival game. The supplied image is a STYLE AND IDENTITY REFERENCE, not a layout to reproduce. Transform the selected reference weapons into clean directional sprite studies. Preserve the weapon identities and tactical olive, charcoal, ivory metal material language, but simplify for genuinely readable small sprites.
STRICT LAYOUT: exactly EIGHT equally spaced COLUMNS, with direction order left-to-right E, SE, S, SW, W, NW, N, NE. That is right, down-right, down, down-left, left, up-left, up, up-right in screen coordinates. Maintain ONE fixed overhead camera elevation; weapon turns in the ground plane. E points right, N points upwards. Views toward/away from camera should show appropriate barrel/stock foreshortening, not eight copies of the same side view. Do NOT rotate the camera. Each row depicts exactly the SAME weapon eight times, one distinct aim direction per cell. All cell centers perfectly aligned on a uniform rectangular grid. Main grip/hold point centered in each cell; point or muzzle extends along the specified direction. Entire weapon stays within central 76% of its cell. Absolutely no cropped silhouettes, overlap, captions, grid lines, frames, angle arrows, drop shadows, hands, people, bullets, rays, attacks, backdrop or text.
PAIRED RESOLUTIONS: each weapon has TWO successive rows: first is a coarse, very simple 16×16 logical pixel interpretation (roughly 10–13 pixels along longest body dimension), second is a separately refined 32×32 interpretation (roughly 20–26 pixels along longest dimension). Both rows have the SAME apparent physical size on the atlas: row16 uses visibly larger square pixels; row32 uses finer pixels and more useful detail. Pixel-aligned jagged contours, hard nearest-neighbor edges, flat limited palettes, no smoothing, gradients, painterly rendering or bloom. 16 rows use about12 colors;32 rows about20. Small dark outline to separate shapes. True transparent alpha outside the sprites.
This atlas is for native sprite export; row/column count, spacing and facing accuracy matter more than presentation.
ATLAS A: exactly SIX ROWS × EIGHT COLUMNS =48 isolated sprites. Landscape rectangular sheet.
Rows1/2: AF01 service pistol, Normal. Very short rectangular silver steel slide, olive dark pistol grip, tiny warm ivory muzzle. A simple compact handgun, no long rifle, no laser.
Rows3/4: AR01 fragmentation grenade, Normal. Segmented olive oval body, silver lever/loop and white band. Lever and pin orientation turn consistently through eight directions, body remains compact.
Rows5/6: CC04 containment katana, Raro. Long gently curved ivory steel blade, small rectangular pale guard, dark wrapped two-part grip; tiny blue mark close to guard, not a fully glowing blade.
Odd rows1/3/5 are16 logical designs, even rows2/4/6 are32 logical designs. No extra rows. No additional weapons or texts.

ATLAS B: exactly SIX ROWS × EIGHT COLUMNS =48 isolated sprites. Landscape rectangular sheet.
Rows1/2: IN03 containment flamethrower, Normal. Broad dark nozzle, two small handles, compact ORANGE SIDE tank and a short hose folded against body. Recognizable as a portable industrial flamethrower, no giant backpack.
Rows3/4: FR07 Three Links rifle, Épico. Long slim dark precision rifle with three small ivory barrel guide rings, narrow stock, a very small violet status detail. Distinct slim silhouette, no giant scope. Eight angles preserve the long barrel and where the stock lies.
Rows5/6: PE04 containment missile launcher, Raro. Bulky olive-gray shoulder tube with a hexagonal dark muzzle, shoulder rest, small amber bracket and tiny blue status notch. Clearly thicker than the rifle; not a normal handgun.
Odd rows1/3/5 are16 logical designs, even rows2/4/6 are32 logical designs. No extra rows. No additional weapons or texts.
ALPHA: no soft halo, no painted checkerboard, no ground shadows. Weapon pixels solid opaque with empty fully transparent space between them. Do not imitate the dark background of the reference.

ATLAS C: exactly EIGHT ROWS × EIGHT COLUMNS =64 isolated sprites. Square sheet.
Rows1/2: RU04 recovery crossbow, Raro. A clearly TRANSVERSE steel bow and taut string, dark brown wooden improvised stock, straight bolt rail, tiny blue notch. Preserve the bow arm shape at each facing, not a rifle.
Rows3/4: TE01 laser emitter, Normal. Short practical charcoal-and-ivory handheld emitter with a small cyan lens and compact grip. No bulky fantasy cannon. Reference prism is NOT the desired model here: create a compact laser emitter consistent with the reference materials.
Rows5/6: AN09 borrowed clock, Legendario. Small ivory clock face without numbers inside a square dark containment cage, folded brown leather strap as grip, tiny gold fittings. This is a physical contained instrument, NOT an attack portal, purple orb or magic circle.
Rows7/8: F24 photonic containment blade, Raro, resulting from katana+laser emitter. Preserve the katana's slender physical ivory blade and dark grip, add a SMALL gray emitter at the guard and a narrow cyan inset along one blade edge, tiny blue status notch. The weapon body is not an oversized beam. This is ONE fused weapon, not two loose separate objects.
Odd rows1/3/5/7 are16 logical designs; even rows2/4/6/8 are32 logical designs. Exactly8rows, no extras, no text.
FACING CHECK: for E and NE and SE the shooting tip is to the RIGHT of the grip; for W and NW and SW it is LEFT. For N,NW,NE the tip is ABOVE the grip; for S,SW,SE the tip is BELOW. Crossbow bolt rail/point and laser lens obey this rule. Do NOT keep a frontal muzzle pointing down in the N column. Maintain all8rows and8columns, no cell omissions. Flat hard alpha with no halos.
correctionB:
Targeted correction of this TRANSPARENT 6-row by8-column pixel weapon atlas. Keep exactly48sprite cells, same identities, materials, row positions,16/32paired detail and spacing. Preserve ALL middle rifle sprites and columns1–5 of every other row. DO NOT add labels, backgrounds or rows.
Only correct columns6,7,8 in rows1,2 (flamethrower) and rows5,6 (missile launcher): they must aim NW,N,NE respectively in SCREEN coordinates. Currently their large dark muzzles still face down/front, which is wrong.
For column6, the firing tip MUST lie at the UPPER LEFT of its grip and stock. For column7, the firing tip MUST be at the TOP of the cell and the grip/stock are BELOW it. For column8, the firing tip MUST be at the UPPER RIGHT of its grip and stock.
Use a fixed steep overhead game camera. In these rear-facing views show the TOP/BACK of the weapon, NOT the large forward-facing muzzle opening at the bottom. A north-facing launcher looks like a narrow vertical tube with its firing end at TOP, a rear cap/shoulder rest toward BOTTOM and grip at center; no front-facing circular hole at bottom. A north-facing flamethrower has its nozzle at TOP and its side orange tank next to its central receiver.
This is not a camera orbit: rotate the actual weapon orientation in the map plane. Keep odd rows coarse16logical, even rows finer32logical. True empty transparency outside crisp opaque sprite pixels; no glow, shadow or soft halo.
